<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NEWPORT CORPORATION</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">January&nbsp;3, 2015</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">be at risk for any currency related fluctuations.&#160; Changes in fair values and transaction gains and losses are included in interest and other expense, net in the results of operations (see Note 6).</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Cash and Cash Equivalents and Marketable Securities</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company considers cash and highly liquid investments with an original maturity of three months or less at the date of purchase to be cash equivalents.&#160; Investments with original maturities exceeding three months at the date of purchase are classified as marketable securities.&#160; All marketable securities are classified as available for sale and are recorded at market value using the specific identification method; unrealized gains and losses are reflected in accumulated other comprehensive loss unless the Company determines there is an other-than-temporary impairment, in which case the loss is recorded in the consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive income (loss).</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Restricted Cash</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has certain agreements, which require it to maintain specified cash balances as collateral.&#160; Such amounts have been classified as restricted cash.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Accounts Receivable</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company records reserves for specific receivables deemed to be at risk for collection, as well as a reserve based on its historical collections experience. The Company estimates the collectability of customer receivables on an ongoing basis by reviewing past due invoices and assessing the current creditworthiness of each customer.&#160; A considerable amount of judgment is required in assessing the ultimate realization of these receivables.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Concentrations of Credit Risk</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financial instruments that potentially subject the Company to concentrations of credit risk consist primarily of cash and cash equivalents, marketable securities, foreign currency exchange contracts and accounts receivable.&#160; The Company maintains cash and cash equivalents with and purchases its foreign currency exchange contracts from major financial institutions and performs periodic evaluations of the relative credit standing of these financial institutions in order to limit the amount of credit exposure with any one institution.&#160; Substantially all of the Company&#146;s marketable securities were invested in certificates of deposit as of January&nbsp;3, 2015.&#160; The Company&#146;s senior financial management and the Company&#146;s Board of Directors periodically review any significant balances of marketable securities to determine the appropriate investment strategy.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s customers are concentrated in the scientific research, defense and security, microelectronics, life and health sciences and industrial markets, and their ability to pay may be influenced by the prevailing macroeconomic conditions present in these markets.&#160; Receivables from the Company&#146;s customers are generally unsecured.&#160; To reduce the overall risk of collection, the Company performs ongoing evaluations of its customers&#146; financial condition.&#160; For the years ended January&nbsp;3, 2015, December&nbsp;28, 2013 and December&nbsp;29, 2012, no customer accounted for 10% or more of the Company&#146;s net sales or 10% or more of the Company&#146;s gross accounts receivable as of the end of such year.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Pension Plans</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Several of the Company&#146;s non-U.S. subsidiaries have defined benefit pension plans covering substantially all full-time employees at those subsidiaries.&#160; Some of the plans are unfunded, as permitted under the plans and applicable laws.&#160; For financial reporting purposes, the calculation of net periodic pension costs is based upon a number of actuarial assumptions, including a discount rate for plan obligations, an assumed rate of return on pension plan assets and an assumed rate of compensation increase for employees covered by the plan.&#160; All of these assumptions are based upon management&#146;s judgment, considering all known trends and uncertainties.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company accounts for its Israeli pension plans using the shut-down method of accounting.&#160; Under the shut-down method, the liability is calculated as if it was payable as of each balance sheet date, on an undiscounted basis.&#160; In addition, the assets and liabilities of the plans are accounted for on a gross basis.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-8<a name="PB_8_185844_5335"></a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NEWPORT CORPORATION</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">January&nbsp;3, 2015</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Inventories</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Inventories are stated at the lower of cost (determined on a first-in, first-out (FIFO) basis) or fair market value and include materials, labor and manufacturing overhead.&#160; Inventories that are expected to be sold within one year are classified as current inventories and are included in inventories<i>,</i> and inventories that the Company expects to hold for longer than one year are included in investments and other assets.&#160; The Company writes down excess and obsolete inventory to net realizable value.&#160; Once the Company writes down the carrying value of inventory, a new cost basis is established, and the Company does not increase the newly established cost basis based on subsequent changes in facts and circumstances.&#160; In assessing the ultimate realization of inventories, the Company makes judgments as to future demand requirements and compares those requirements with the current or committed inventory levels.&#160; The Company records any amounts required to reduce the carrying value of inventory to net realizable value as a charge to cost of sales.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Property and Equipment</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Property and equipment are stated at cost, less accumulated depreciation.&#160; Depreciation expense includes amortization of assets under capital leases.&#160; Depreciation is recorded on a straight-line basis over the estimated useful lives of the assets as follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Leasehold improvements are amortized over the shorter of their estimated useful life or the remaining lease term.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Capitalized Software Costs</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All direct costs related to developing internal use software during the application development stage are capitalized and amortized using the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of the assets.&#160; Costs incurred in the preliminary project stage, maintenance costs and training costs are expensed as incurred.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Intangible Assets, including Goodwill</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Developed technology is amortized on a straight line basis over 10 to 20 years, depending on the life of the product technology.&#160; Intangible assets related to customer relationships are primarily amortized over a period of up to 10 years on an accelerated basis.&#160; In-process research and development is amortized on a straight line basis over the product&#146;s estimated useful life upon completion of the technology.&#160; Other intangible assets include acquired backlog, product trademarks and trade names, non-competition agreements and defensible assets.&#160; With the exception of product trademarks and trade names, such assets are amortized on a straight line basis over a period of three months to 10 years, depending on the asset.&#160; Trademarks and trade names associated with products are amortized on a straight line basis over the estimated remaining life of the product technology, which ranges from 10 to 20 years.&#160; Trademarks and trade names associated with a business have indefinite lives and are not amortized.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Goodwill represents the excess of the purchase price of the net assets of acquired entities over the fair value of such assets.&#160; Under Accounting Standards Codification (ASC) 350,&nbsp;<i>Intangibles &#150; Goodwill and Other, </i>goodwill and other indefinite-lived intangible assets are not amortized but are tested for impairment at least annually or when circumstances exist that would indicate an impairment of such goodwill or other intangible assets.&#160; The Company performs the annual impairment test as of the beginning of the fourth quarter of each year.&#160; A two-step test is used to identify the potential impairment and to measure the amount of impairment, if any.&#160; The first step is based upon a comparison of the fair value of each of the Company&#146;s reporting units, as defined, and the carrying value of the reporting unit&#146;s net assets, including goodwill.&#160; If the fair value of the reporting unit exceeds its carrying value, goodwill is considered not to be impaired; otherwise, step two is required.&#160; Under step two, the implied fair value of goodwill, calculated as the difference between the fair value of the reporting unit and the fair value of the net assets of the reporting unit, is compared with the carrying value of goodwill.&#160; The excess of the carrying value of goodwill over the implied fair value represents the amount impaired.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-9<a name="PB_9_185936_5796"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NEWPORT CORPORATION</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">January&nbsp;3, 2015</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company determines its reporting units by identifying those operating segments or components for which discrete financial information is available which is regularly reviewed by the management of that unit.&#160; For any acquisition, the Company allocates goodwill to the applicable reporting unit at the completion of the purchase price allocation through specific identification.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fair value of the Company&#146;s reporting units is determined using a combination of a comparative company analysis and a discounted cash flow analysis.&#160; The comparative company analysis establishes fair value by applying market multiples to the Company&#146;s revenue and earnings before interest, income taxes, depreciation and amortization.&#160; Such multiples are determined by comparing the Company&#146;s reporting units with other publicly traded companies within the respective industries that have similar economic characteristics.&#160; In addition, a control premium is added to reflect the value an investor would pay to obtain a controlling interest, which is consistent with the lower quartile control premium for transactions in those industries in which the Company does business.&#160; The discounted cash flow analysis establishes fair value by estimating the present value of the projected future cash flows of each reporting unit and applying a terminal growth rate.&#160; The present value of estimated discounted future cash flows is determined using the Company&#146;s estimates of revenue and costs for the reporting units, using a combination of historical results, industry data and competitor data, as well as appropriate discount rates.&#160; The discount rate is determined using a weighted-average cost of capital that incorporates market participant data and a risk premium applicable to each reporting unit.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2012, </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">sales by the Company&#146;s former Ophir Division were below the levels that the Company had originally forecasted at the time of the acquisition of Ophir Optronics,&nbsp;Ltd. and its subsidiaries (Ophir).&#160; In light of those sales levels and other factors, </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">in connection with the annual evaluation of goodwill and other intangible assets in the fourth quarter of 2012, </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">the Company determined that the cash flow projections of its former Ophir Division had diminished and, therefore, the goodwill and other intangible assets associated with that division were impaired.&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result, the Company recorded an impairment charge of $67.8 million, which represented all of the goodwill that had been allocated to the Ophir Division.&#160; In addition, the Company recorded an impairment charge of $62.6 million related to acquired intangible assets.&#160; Such charge consisted of $33.8 million for customer relationships, $21.5&nbsp;million for developed technology, $2.1 million for in-process research and development, $4.6 million for indefinite-lived trade names and $0.6 million for finite-lived trade names.&#160; Trade names and developed technologies were valued using the relief-from-royalty method, and customer relationships and in-process research and development were valued using the multi-period excess earnings method.&#160; There were no impairment charges in 2014 or 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Long-Lived Assets</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company assesses the impairment of long-lived assets, other than goodwill and other indefinite-lived intangible assets, to determine if their carrying value may not be recoverable.&#160; The determination of related estimated useful lives and whether or not these assets are impaired involves significant judgments, related primarily to the future profitability and/or future value of the assets.&#160; Changes in the Company&#146;s strategic plan and/or other-than-temporary changes in market conditions could significantly impact these judgments and could require adjustments to recorded asset balances.&#160; Long-lived assets are evaluated for impairment at least annually, as well as whenever an event or change in circumstances has occurred that could have a significant adverse effect on the fair value of long-lived assets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the fourth quarter of 2012, in connection with the Company&#146;s annual evaluation of long-lived assets, it determined that certain assets of its former Ophir Division (which are now a part of the Company&#146;s Photonics Group) were impaired.&#160; Accordingly, the Company recorded an impairment charge of $0.5 million related to fixed assets.&#160; There were no impairment charges during 2014 or 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Warranty</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Unless otherwise stated in the Company&#146;s product literature or in its agreements with customers, products sold by the Company&#146;s Photonics and Optics Groups generally carry a one-year warranty from the original invoice date on all product materials and workmanship, other than filters and gratings products, which generally carry a 90-day warranty, and laser beam profilers and dental CAD/CAM scanners, which generally carry a two-year warranty.&#160; Products sold by the Photonics and Optics Groups to original equipment manufacturer (OEM) customers carry </font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-10<a name="PB_10_190012_2897"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NEWPORT CORPORATION</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">January&nbsp;3, 2015</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">warranties generally ranging from 15 to 19 months.&#160; Products sold by the Company&#146;s Lasers Group carry warranties that vary by product, customer type and product component, but generally range from 90 days to two years.&#160; In certain cases, such warranties for Lasers Group products are limited by either a set time period or a maximum amount of hourly usage of the product, whichever occurs first.&#160; Defective products will be either repaired or replaced, generally at the Company&#146;s option, upon meeting certain criteria.&#160; The Company accrues a provision for the estimated costs that may be incurred for warranties relating to a product (based on historical experience) as a component of cost of sales.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Environmental Reserves</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company accrues for losses associated with environmental remediation obligations when such losses are probable and reasonably estimable.&#160; Accruals for estimated losses from environmental remediation obligations generally are recognized no later than completion of the remedial feasibility study.&#160; Such accruals are adjusted as further information develops or circumstances change.&#160; Costs of future expenditures are discounted to their present value.&#160; Recoveries of environmental remediation costs from other parties are recognized as assets when their receipt is deemed probable.&#160; See Note 10 for additional information.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Revenue Recognition</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company recognizes revenue after title to and risk of loss of products have passed to the customer, or delivery of the service has been completed, provided that persuasive evidence of an arrangement exists, the price is fixed or determinable and collectability is reasonably assured.&#160; Title to and risk of loss of products generally pass to the customer upon delivery (either at point of shipment or destination depending on the contractual delivery terms), but in certain cases pass upon acceptance.&#160; The Company recognizes revenue and related costs for arrangements with multiple deliverables as each element is delivered or completed based upon the lesser of its relative selling price, determined based upon the price that would be charged on a standalone basis, or the amount contractually due upon delivery of each element.&#160; If a portion of the total contract price is not payable until installation is complete, the Company does not recognize such portion as revenue until completion of installation.&#160; Multiple deliverable sales frequently involve ancillary services such as installation, extended warranties or service contracts.&#160; Such services are not often sold by the Company or its competitors on a stand-alone basis.&#160; Therefore, the Company calculates the estimated selling price based on specific facts and circumstances for each service.&#160; For example, the relative selling price for installation is determined by estimating the installation hours for a particular product, using historical experience, multiplied by the standard service billing rate.&#160; Revenue for extended service contracts is recognized over the related contract periods.&#160; Revenue for programs involving design and development services and delivery of product prototypes and/or other deliverables is recognized upon the completion of specified milestones, or over the term of the program based upon the percentage of completion of the program (using the cost-to-cost method), depending on the terms of the associated contract.&#160; Certain sales to international customers are made through third-party distributors and revenue is recognized upon the sale to the distributor.&#160; A discount below list price is generally provided at the time the product is sold to the distributor, and such discount is reflected as a reduction in net sales.&#160; Freight costs billed to customers are included in net sales, and freight costs incurred are included in <i>selling, general and administrative expenses</i>.&#160; Sales taxes collected from customers are recorded on a net basis and any amounts not yet remitted to tax authorities are included in <i>accrued expenses and other current liabilities</i>.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Customers (including distributors) generally have 30 days from the original invoice date (generally 60 days for international customers) to return a standard catalog product purchase for exchange or credit.&#160; Catalog products must be returned in the original condition and meet certain other criteria.&#160; Custom, option-configured and certain other products as defined in the terms and conditions of sale cannot be returned without the Company&#146;s consent.&#160; For certain products, the Company establishes a sales return reserve based on the historical product returns.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Advertising</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company expenses the costs of advertising as incurred.&#160; Advertising costs, including the costs of the Company&#146;s participation at industry trade shows, totaled $4.4 million, $4.2 million and $3.9 million for 2014, 2013 and 2012, respectively.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Shipping and Handling Costs</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company expenses the costs of shipping and handling as incurred.&#160; Shipping and handling costs of $5.0&nbsp;million, $4.7 million and $5.2 million are included in <i>selling, general and administrative expenses</i> for 2014, 2013 and 2012, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Research and Development</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All research and development costs are expensed as incurred.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Non-Controlling Interests</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In October&nbsp;2011, the Company acquired Ophir.&#160; As of December&nbsp;28, 2013, Ophir&#146;s subsidiaries, Ophir Japan,&nbsp;Ltd. in Japan, Ophir Optronics GmbH in Germany, and Optical Metrology Ltd. in Israel, had non-controlling interest holders of 33.3%, 25% and 14.1%, respectively.&#160; Earnings (losses) attributable to the non-controlling interests are separately identified in the Company&#146;s consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2014, the Company purchased all shares owned by the holders of the non-controlling interests in Optical Metrology Ltd., Ophir Japan Ltd. and Ophir Optronics GmbH, for $0.9 million, $0.9&nbsp;million and $0.2 million, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company utilizes the asset and liability method of accounting for income taxes.&#160; Deferred income taxes are recognized for the future tax consequences of temporary differences using enacted statutory tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled.&#160; Temporary differences include the difference between the financial statement carrying amounts, and the tax bases of existing assets and liabilities as well as operating loss and tax credit carryforwards.&#160; In accordance with the provisions of ASC 740,&nbsp;<i>Income Taxes</i>, a valuation allowance for deferred tax assets is recorded to the extent the Company cannot determine that the ultimate realization of the net deferred tax assets is more likely than not.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company utilizes ASC 740-10-25,&nbsp;<i>Income Taxes - Recognition</i>, for the recognition, measurement and disclosure of uncertain tax positions.&#160; Under ASC 740-10-25, income tax positions must meet the more-likely-than-not threshold to be recognized in the financial statements.&#160; The Company&#146;s policy is to record interest and penalties associated with unrecognized tax benefits as income tax expense.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Income (loss) per Share</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Basic income (loss) per share is computed by dividing net income (loss) by the weighted-average number of shares of common stock outstanding during the period.&#160; Diluted income per share is computed using the weighted-average number of shares of common stock outstanding during the period plus the dilutive effects of common stock equivalents (restricted stock units, stock options and stock appreciation rights) outstanding during the period, determined using the treasury stock method.&#160; Diluted loss per share excludes the antidilutive effects of common stock equivalents outstanding during the periods.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Stock-Based Compensation</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company accounts for stock-based compensation in accordance with ASC 718, <i>Compensation &#150; Stock Compensation</i>.&#160; Under the fair value recognition provision of ASC 718, stock-based compensation cost is estimated at the grant date based on the fair value of the award.&#160; The Company estimates the fair value of stock appreciation rights granted using the Black-Scholes-Merton option pricing model and a single option award approach.&#160; The fair value of restricted stock unit awards is based on the closing market price of the Company&#146;s common stock on the date of grant.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Determining the appropriate fair value of stock appreciation rights at the grant date requires significant judgment, including estimating the volatility of the Company&#146;s common stock and expected term of the awards.&#160; The Company computes expected volatility based on historical volatility over the expected term.&#160; The expected term represents the </font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-12<a name="PB_12_190110_7748"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NEWPORT CORPORATION</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">January&nbsp;3, 2015</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">period of time that stock appreciation rights are expected to be outstanding and is determined based on historical experience, giving consideration to the contractual terms of the stock-based awards, vesting schedules and expected exercise behavior.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A substantial portion of the Company&#146;s restricted stock unit awards vest based upon the achievement of one or more financial performance thresholds established by the Compensation Committee of the Company&#146;s Board of Directors.&#160; Currently, such performance thresholds relate to the fiscal year in which the award is granted, and if and to the extent that such performance thresholds are met, the awards vest in equal one-third (1/3) annual installments.&#160; Until the Company has determined that performance thresholds have been met, the amount of expense that the Company records relating to performance-based awards is estimated based on the likelihood of achieving the performance thresholds.&#160; The amount of expense recorded by the Company is also based on estimated forfeitures.&#160; The fair value of stock-based awards, adjusted for estimated forfeitures (and adjusted for estimated or actual achievement of performance thresholds in the case of awards having performance-based vesting conditions), is amortized using the straight-line attribution method over the requisite service period of the award, which is generally the vesting period.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Use of Estimates</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts reported in the financial statements and accompanying notes.&#160; Actual results could differ from those estimates.&#160; Significant estimates made in preparing the consolidated financial statements include (but are not limited to) those related to revenue recognition, the allowance for doubtful accounts, inventory reserves, warranty obligations, pension plans, asset impairment valuations, income tax valuations, and stock-based compensation expenses.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Recent Accounting Pronouncements</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In April&nbsp;2014, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) issued Accounting Standards Update (ASU) No.&nbsp;2014-08, <i>Presentation of Financial Statements and Property, Plant and Equipment: Reporting Discontinued Operations and Disclosures of Disposal of Components of an Entity</i>, which updates the guidance in Topics 205 and 360.&#160; ASU No.&nbsp;2014-08 requires that the disposal of a component of an entity or a group of components of an entity be reported in discontinued operations if the disposal represents a strategic shift that has or will have a major effect on the entity&#146;s operations and financial results.&#160; ASU No.&nbsp;2014-08 also requires additional disclosures regarding discontinued operations.&#160; ASU No.&nbsp;2014-08 is required to be applied prospectively for fiscal years and interim periods beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2014.&#160; The adoption of ASU No.&nbsp;2014-08 will not have a material impact on the Company&#146;s financial position or results of operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In May&nbsp;2014, the FASB issued ASU No.&nbsp;2014-09, <i>Revenue from Contracts with Customers</i>, which created Topic 606.&#160; ASU No.&nbsp;2014-09 establishes a core principle that a company should recognize revenue to depict the transfer of promised goods or services to a customer in an amount that reflects the consideration to which the company expects to be entitled in exchange for those goods or services.&#160; In order to achieve that core principle, companies are required to apply the following steps: (1)&nbsp;identify the contract with the customer; (2)&nbsp;identify performance obligations in the contract; (3)&nbsp;determine the transaction price; (4)&nbsp;allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations in the contract; and (5)&nbsp;recognize revenue when (or as) the company satisfies a performance obligation.&#160; ASU No.&nbsp;2014-09 will become effective for interim and annual periods beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2016 and can be applied either (i)&nbsp;retrospectively to each prior reporting period, or (ii)&nbsp;retrospectively with the cumulative effect of initial application recognized on the date of adoption.&#160; Early adoption is not permitted.&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is currently evaluating the expected impact of ASU No.&nbsp;2014-09 on its financial position and results of operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In August&nbsp;2014, the FASB issued ASU No.&nbsp;2014-15, <i>Disclosure of Uncertainties about an Entity&#146;s Ability to Continue as a Going Concern</i>, which provides guidance on management&#146;s responsibility in evaluating whether there is substantial doubt about a company&#146;s ability to continue as a going concern and to provide related footnote disclosures.&#160; ASU No.&nbsp;2014-15 will become effective for annual periods beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2016 and early adoption is permitted.&#160; The adoption of ASU No.&nbsp;2014-15 will not have an impact on the Company&#146;s financial position or results of operations.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-13<a name="PB_13_190128_141"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NEWPORT CORPORATION</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">January&nbsp;3, 2015</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In November&nbsp;2014, the FASB issued ASU No.&nbsp;2014-17, <i>Pushdown Accounting, </i>which provides acquired companies an option to apply pushdown accounting to its separate financial statements upon an event resulting in a change in control.&#160; An election to apply pushdown accounting in a period subsequent to the change in control event would be considered a change in accounting principle.&#160; ASU No.&nbsp;2014-17 became effective on November&nbsp;18, 2014 and did not have an impact on the Company&#146;s financial position or results of operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In January&nbsp;2015, the FASB issued ASU No.&nbsp;2015-1, <i>Simplifying Income Statement Presentation by Eliminating the Concept of Extraordinary Items.</i>&#160; ASU No.&nbsp;2015-1 eliminates the concept of extraordinary items, which previously required companies to present extraordinary items in the income statement net of tax, after income from continuing operations.&#160; ASU No.&nbsp;2015-1 will become effective for annual and interim periods beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2015 and early adoption is permitted.&#160; The adoption of ASU No.&nbsp;2015-1 will not have an impact on the Company&#146;s financial position or results of operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 2&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; ACQUISITIONS AND DIVESTITURES</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Acquisition of FEMTOLASERS</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February&nbsp;11, 2015, the Company acquired all of the capital stock of FEMTOLASERS Produktions GmbH (FEMTOLASERS).&#160;&#160; The initial purchase price of &#128;9.1 million (approximately $10.9 million) was paid in cash at closing and is subject to a net asset adjustment.&#160; Of the initial purchase price, &#128;2.3 million was deposited at closing into escrow until thirty months after closing, to secure certain obligations of the FEMTOLASERS selling shareholders under the share purchase agreement.&#160; The Company incurred $0.3 million in transaction costs, which have been expensed as incurred and are included in <i>selling, general and administrative expenses</i> in the accompanying statements of operations and comprehensive income (loss).&#160; FEMTOLASERS expands the Company&#146;s offering of ultrafast laser products and enhances its technology base in this area.&#160; The results of FEMTOLASERS will be included in the results of the Company&#146;s Lasers Group as of the acquisition date.&#160; The Company has not disclosed the fair value of assets and liabilities acquired or supplemental pro forma financial information for this acquisition, as the initial accounting for this transaction has not been completed.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Immediately following the closing of the transaction, the Company repaid &#128;3.6 million (approximately $4.4 million) of FEMTOLASERS&#146; outstanding loans that were assumed as part of the acquisition.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Acquisition of V-Gen</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On September&nbsp;29, 2014, the Company acquired all of the capital stock of V-Gen,&nbsp;Ltd. (V-Gen). The purchase price was $36.4&nbsp;million, of which $35.6 million was allocated to the purchase price and $0.8 million was allocated to the fair value of unearned compensation related to unvested stock options.&#160; The purchase price was paid in cash and consisted of an initial purchase price of $34.0 million, plus an adjustment of $2.4&nbsp;million based on a calculation of V-Gen&#146;s net working capital and cash balances at the closing date.&#160; After considering the cash held by V-Gen as of the closing date, the net cash used by the Company for this transaction was $34.1 million. The Company incurred $0.3 million in transaction costs, which have been expensed as incurred and are included in <i>selling, general and administrative expenses</i> in the accompanying statements of operations and comprehensive income (loss).&#160; V-Gen expands the Company&#146;s fiber laser products and its technology in this area.&#160; The results of V-Gen are included in the results of the Company&#146;s Lasers Group.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The consideration paid by the Company for the acquisition of V-Gen is allocated to the assets acquired, net of the liabilities assumed, based upon their estimated fair values as of the date of the acquisition.&nbsp; The excess of the purchase price over the estimated fair value of the assets acquired, net of the estimated fair value of the liabilities assumed, is recorded as goodwill.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-14<a name="PB_14_190145_7608"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the purposes of determining pro forma net income, adjustments were made to actual net income of the Company for both periods presented in the table above.&nbsp; The pro forma net income assumes amortization of acquired intangible assets began at the beginning of 2013 rather than on September&nbsp;29, 2014.&nbsp; The result is a net increase in amortization expense of $0.7 million and $1.2 million for the years ended January&nbsp;3, 2015 and December&nbsp;28, 2013, respectively.&nbsp; In addition, $0.3 million in charges to cost of sales related to inventory that was marked up to fair value for purchase accounting was added back to pro forma net income for the year ended January&nbsp;3, 2015 and subtracted from pro forma net income for the year ended December&nbsp;28, 2013.&nbsp; Transaction costs totaling $0.3&nbsp;million, which were incurred prior to the closing of the acquisition, are excluded from pro forma net income.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NEWPORT CORPORATION</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">January&nbsp;3, 2015</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Divestiture of Advanced Packaging Systems Business</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the third quarter of 2013, the Company developed a plan to sell its advanced packaging systems business and, based on negotiations for the sale of this business that occurred during the second half of 2013, the Company considered the assets and liabilities of this business as held for sale as of December&nbsp;28, 2013.&nbsp; The Company completed the sale of this business in January&nbsp;2014 for $5.7 million, consisting of an initial purchase price of $6.0 million, less an adjustment of $0.3 million based on the net assets of the business at closing.&#160; The initial purchase price consisted of $5.35 million in cash and an unsecured note receivable of $0.65 million, and the net asset adjustment was repaid to the purchaser in cash.&#160; The Company incurred $0.4 million in transaction costs, which have been expensed as incurred and are included in <i>selling, general and administrative expenses </i>in the accompanying consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive income (loss).</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The net book value of this business was $9.5 million as of December&nbsp;28, 2013; however, because these assets were held for sale at such time, the Company wrote them down to their net realizable value as of December&nbsp;28, 2013 based on the terms that had been negotiated with the purchaser and expected transaction costs, resulting in a loss of $4.7 million during 2013.&#160; In 2014, the Company recorded a gain of $0.4 million to reduce the loss on the sale to $4.3 million, based on the final terms of the transaction and the net assets of the business on the closing date.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Acquisition of Vistek Assets</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;10, 2012, the Company acquired substantially all of the assets of Advanced Vibration Technologies,&nbsp;Inc., a corporation doing business under the trade name of Vistek (Vistek), for a purchase price of $2.5 million.&#160; The purchase price was paid in cash at closing, of which $0.25 million was deposited at closing into escrow until October&nbsp;10, 2013, to secure certain indemnification obligations of Vistek and its sole shareholder under the asset purchase agreement.&#160; The full amount of the escrow deposit was released to the seller upon the expiration of the escrow.&#160; The Company incurred $49 thousand in transaction costs, which have been expensed as incurred and are included in <i>selling, general and administrative expenses </i>in the accompanying consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive income (loss).&#160; This acquisition expanded the Company&#146;s vibration control product offerings.&#160; The results of the Vistek business are included in the results of the Company&#146;s Photonics Group.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Acquisition of ILX</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;13, 2012, the Company acquired all of the outstanding capital stock of ILX Lightwave Corporation (ILX) by means of a merger of a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company with and into ILX.&#160; The total purchase price for the acquisition was $9.0 million.&#160; An initial purchase price of $9.3 million was paid in cash at closing, of which $1.2 million was deposited at closing into escrow until July&nbsp;12, 2013, to secure certain indemnification and other obligations of the ILX securityholders.&#160; The purchase price was subsequently reduced by $0.3 million, based on a calculation of ILX&#146;s net assets at closing.&#160; The full amount of the escrow deposit was released to the ILX securityholders upon the expiration of the escrow.&#160; The Company incurred $0.1 million in transaction costs, which have been expensed as incurred and are included in <i>selling, general and administrative expenses </i>in the accompanying consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive income (loss).&#160; This acquisition expanded the Company&#146;s optical power meter, laser diode instrumentation and fiber optic source product offerings, and added laser diode and light emitting diode (LED) burn-in, test and characterization systems to its product portfolio.&#160; The results of ILX are included in the results of the Company&#146;s Photonics Group.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-16<a name="PB_16_195240_7056"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2014, the Company determined that it would no longer utilize certain software applications for which it had capitalized the application development costs and recognized a loss of $2.3 million on the disposal of such assets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Depreciation expense, including the amortization of assets under capital leases, totaled $17.1 million, $17.2 million and $18.2 million for 2014, 2013 and 2012, respectively.&#160; At December&nbsp;28, 2013, assets under capital leases were $0.9 million, net of accumulated amortization of $1.8 million.&#160; At January&nbsp;3, 2015, there were no material capital leases.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Accrued Warranty Obligations</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Short-term accrued warranty obligations, which expire within one year, are included in <i>accrued expenses and other current liabilities</i> and long-term warranty obligations are included in <i>deferred income taxes and other liabilities</i> in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 7</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">STOCK INCENTIVE PLANS AND STOCK-BASED COMPENSATION</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Stock-Based Benefit Plans</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In March&nbsp;2011, the Company&#146;s Board of Directors adopted the 2011 Stock Incentive Plan (2011 Plan) subject to approval of its stockholders, which was received in May&nbsp;2011.&#160; The primary purpose of the 2011 Plan is to enhance the Company&#146;s ability to attract, motivate and retain the services of qualified employees, officers and directors, consultants and other service providers upon whose judgment, initiative and efforts the successful conduct and development of the Company&#146;s business largely depends.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The 2011 Plan authorizes the Company to grant up to 6,000,000 shares of common stock.&#160; This number of shares is subject to adjustments as to the number and kind of shares in the event of stock splits, stock dividends or certain other similar changes in the capital structure of the Company.&#160; Upon approval of the 2011 Plan by the Company&#146;s stockholders, the Company&#146;s 2006 Performance-Based Stock Incentive Plan was terminated for purposes of future grants, and only the 6,000,000 shares authorized for issuance under the 2011 Plan remained available for future grants.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The 2011 Plan permits the grant of stock appreciation rights, restricted stock, restricted stock units, incentive stock options and non-qualified stock options.&#160; For purposes of calculating the total number of shares that may be issued under the 2011 Plan, the 2011 Plan provides that &#147;full value&#148; awards shall be counted against the share limit to a greater extent than &#147;appreciation&#148; awards.&#160; Stock options and stock appreciation rights, which are &#147;appreciation&#148; awards, shall be counted against the share limit under the 2011 Plan as one (1)&nbsp;share for each share of common stock subject to such award.&#160; Restricted stock and restricted stock units, which are &#147;full value&#148; awards, shall be counted against the share limit under the 2011 Plan as one and seven tenths (1.7) shares for each share of common stock subject to such award.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Any stock options or stock appreciation rights granted under the 2011 Plan will have exercise prices or base values not less than the fair market value of the Company&#146;s common stock on the date of grant and terms of not more than seven years.&#160; The vesting of substantially all awards granted to directors under the 2011 Plan occurs over a period of one year.&#160; The vesting of substantially all awards granted to officers and employees under the 2011 Plan occurs over a period of three years, and the vesting of substantially all restricted stock unit awards is also conditioned upon the achievement of performance thresholds established by the Compensation Committee of the Company&#146;s Board of Directors.&#160; Currently, such performance thresholds relate to the fiscal year in which the award is granted, and if and to the extent that such performance thresholds are met, the awards vest in equal one-third (1/3) annual installments.&#160; All awards are subject to forfeiture if employment or other service terminates prior to the vesting of the awards.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company maintains an Employee Stock Purchase Plan (Purchase Plan) to provide employees of the Company with an opportunity to purchase common stock through payroll deductions.&#160; The Purchase Plan allows employees to </font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Stock-Based Compensation Expense</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As required by ASC 718, the Company estimates the expected future forfeitures of stock appreciation rights and restricted stock units and recognizes compensation expense for only those equity awards expected to vest, excluding the expected future forfeitures.&#160; If actual forfeitures differ from the Company&#146;s estimates, the amount of compensation expense recognized for the applicable period is cumulatively adjusted.&#160; The Company assumed a forfeiture rate of 12.5% in recognizing compensation expense for 2014, 2013 and 2012.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At January&nbsp;3, 2015, the total compensation cost related to unvested stock-based awards granted to employees, officers and directors under the Company&#146;s stock-based benefit plans that had not yet been recognized was $16.4 million, net of estimated forfeitures.&#160; This future compensation expense will be amortized, using the straight-line attribution method over a weighted-average period of 1.8 years.&#160; The actual compensation expense that the Company will recognize in the future related to stock-based awards outstanding at January&nbsp;3, 2015 will be adjusted for subsequent forfeitures.&#160; All performance conditions applicable to stock-based awards outstanding at January&nbsp;3, 2015 have been met.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The intrinsic value of stock appreciation rights exercised during fiscal years 2014, 2013 and 2012 totaled $1.7 million, $2.0&nbsp;million and $1.3 million, respectively.&#160; The intrinsic value of stock appreciation rights exercised is calculated as the difference between the market price on the date of exercise and the base value, multiplied by the number of stock appreciation rights exercised.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The grant date fair value of stock appreciation rights that vested during fiscal years 2014, 2013 and 2012 totaled $2.8 million, $2.3 million and $1.7 million, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Short-Term Lines of Credit and Loans</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At January&nbsp;3, 2015, the Company had various revolving lines of credit and an agreement with a Japanese bank denominated in yen under which it sells trade notes receivable with recourse.&#160; The revolving lines of credit with Japanese banks allow the Company to borrow up to $5.6 million (based on the currency exchange rate at January&nbsp;3, 2015).&#160; The agreement to sell receivables allows the Company to sell up to $1.7 million of receivables (based on the currency exchange rate at January&nbsp;3, 2015).&#160; The effective interest rates and the amounts outstanding under these lines of credit and agreement at January&nbsp;3, 2015 are presented in the table above.&#160; Such amounts are included in <i>short-term borrowings </i>in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Japanese Bonds</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2011, the Company issued 200 million Japanese yen in private placement bonds through a Japanese bank.&#160; These bonds matured on June&nbsp;30, 2014 and have been repaid.</font></p>
