<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Secured Credit Facility</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In October&nbsp;2011, the Company entered into a credit agreement with certain lenders.&#160; Such credit agreement and the related security agreement provided for a senior secured credit facility consisting of a $185&nbsp;million term loan and a $65 million revolving line of credit, each with a term of five years.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;18, 2013, the Company entered into a new credit agreement with certain lenders (Credit Agreement), which replaced the Company&#146;s prior credit agreement.&#160; The Credit Agreement consists of a senior secured revolving credit facility of $275 million with a term of five years (Credit Facility).&#160; The Credit Agreement also provides the Company with the option to increase the aggregate principal amount of loans in the form of additional revolving loans or a separate tranche of term loans, in an aggregate amount that does not exceed $50 million, in each case subject to certain terms and conditions contained in the Credit Agreement.&#160; Concurrently with the closing of the Credit Agreement, the Company terminated the prior credit agreement after repaying the entire outstanding principal amount of $152.6 million and all accrued interest and fees thereon, utilizing $120.0 million borrowed under the Credit Facility together with a portion of the Company&#146;s then-existing cash balances.&#160; Upon terminating the prior credit agreement, the Company recorded a loss on extinguishment of debt of $3.4 million, to write off the remaining deferred debt issuance costs relating to the prior credit agreement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At January&nbsp;3, 2015, the outstanding balance under the Credit Facility was $71.0 million.&#160; The interest rate per annum applicable to amounts outstanding under the Credit Facility is, at the Company&#146;s option, either (a)&nbsp;the base rate as defined in the Credit Agreement (Base Rate) plus an applicable margin, or (b)&nbsp;the Eurodollar Rate as defined in the Credit Agreement (Eurodollar Rate) plus an applicable margin.&#160; A commitment fee is payable on the unused portion of the Credit Facility.&#160; The margins over the Base Rate and Eurodollar Rate applicable to the loans outstanding under the Credit Facility, and the commitment fee, are adjusted periodically based on the consolidated leverage ratio of the Company, as calculated pursuant to the Credit Agreement.&#160; The maximum applicable margins are 1.25% per annum for Base Rate loans and 2.25% per annum for Eurodollar Rate loans, and the minimum applicable margins are 0.5% per annum for Base Rate loans and 1.5% per annum for Eurodollar Rate loans.&#160; The maximum commitment fee is 0.40% per annum, and the minimum commitment fee is 0.25% per annum.&#160; As of January&nbsp;3, 2015, the interest rate per annum applicable to amounts outstanding under the Credit Facility was 1.69%, and the commitment fee on the unused portion of the Credit Facility was 0.25%.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s obligations under the Credit Agreement are secured by a lien on substantially all of the assets of Newport Corporation and certain of its U.S. subsidiaries, which are guarantors under the Credit Agreement, as well as by a pledge of certain shares of international subsidiaries of Newport Corporation.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Other Loans</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As part of the acquisition of Ophir, the Company assumed certain loans with Israeli and Japanese banks.&#160; The effective interest rates and the principal amounts outstanding under these loans at January&nbsp;3, 2015 are shown in the</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For 2014, 2013 and 2012, 0.6 million, 1.3 million and 1.7 million stock options and/or stock appreciation rights, respectively, were excluded from the computations of diluted net income (loss) per share, as their exercise prices (or base values) exceeded the average market price of the Company&#146;s common stock during such periods, and their inclusion would have been antidilutive.&#160; For 2012, 0.6 million restricted stock units were excluded from the computations of diluted net income (loss) per share, as the amount of unrecognized future compensation expense associated with these restricted stock units would have resulted in assumed proceeds in excess of the amount required to repurchase the underlying shares under the treasury stock method, and, therefore, their inclusion would have been antidilutive.&#160; For 2012, an additional 0.7 million common stock equivalents have been excluded from the denominator for purposes of computing diluted net loss per share, as their inclusion would be antidilutive due to the Company incurring a net loss.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Facility Leases</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company leases certain of its manufacturing and office facilities and equipment under non-cancelable leases, certain of which contain renewal options.&#160; In addition to the base rent, the Company is generally required to pay insurance, real estate taxes and other operating expenses relating to such facilities.&#160; In some cases, base rent increases during the term of the lease based on a predetermined schedule.&#160; The Company recognizes rent expense on a straight-line basis over the life of the lease for leases containing stated rent escalations.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NEWPORT CORPORATION</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">January&nbsp;3, 2015</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">due to releases of hazardous substances during the 1960s and 1970s</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&#160; The site is mature, and investigations and remediation efforts have been ongoing for approximately 30 years.&#160; Spectra-Physics and the other Responsible Parties have entered into a cost-sharing agreement covering the costs of remediating the off-site groundwater contamination, pursuant to which Spectra-Physics is responsible for 30% of the remediation costs.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At the time of the Company&#146;s acquisition of Spectra-Physics, it established a reserve to cover known costs relating to this site for which it was liable, the balance of which was immaterial at January&nbsp;3, 2015 and December&nbsp;28, 2013.&#160; The Company is currently unaware of any material future expenses associated with this site for which the Company will be liable.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Indemnification Obligations</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company from time to time enters into certain types of agreements that contingently require the Company to indemnify the other parties against certain claims.&#160; These contracts primarily include: (i)&nbsp;contracts for the development and/or sale of products, under which the Company customarily agrees to hold the other party harmless against losses arising from bodily injury or damage to personal property caused by the Company&#146;s personnel or products or infringement by the Company&#146;s products of third-party intellectual property rights; (ii)&nbsp;certain real estate leases, under which the Company may be required to indemnify property owners for environmental and other liabilities, and other claims arising from the Company&#146;s use of the applicable premises; (iii)&nbsp;divestiture agreements, under which the Company may provide customary indemnifications to purchasers of the Company&#146;s businesses or assets; and (iv)&nbsp;certain agreements with the Company&#146;s officers, directors and employees, under which the Company may be required to indemnify such persons for liabilities incurred by them in the course of their employment.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In each of these circumstances, payment by the Company is typically subject to the other party making a claim to and cooperating with the Company pursuant to the procedures specified in the particular contract. This usually allows the Company to challenge the other party&#146;s claims and to control the defense or settlement of any third-party claims brought against the other party.&#160; The Company&#146;s obligations under these agreements are typically not limited in terms of amount or duration. In some instances, the Company may have recourse against third parties and/or insurance covering certain payments made by the Company.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">It is not possible to predict the maximum potential amount of future payments under these or similar agreements due to the conditional nature of the Company&#146;s obligations and the unique facts and circumstances involved in each particular agreement.&#160; Historically, the Company has not been obligated to make significant payments for these obligations, and no liabilities have been recorded for these obligations as of January&nbsp;3, 2015 and December&nbsp;28, 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Other Contingencies</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In November&nbsp;2010, two former employees of Spectra-Physics, Linda Pope and Yvette Flores, together with their children, Tia Pope Hudson and Mark Flores, filed a complaint against Spectra-Physics and the Company in the Superior Court for Santa Clara County, California.&#160; Plaintiffs alleged that between 1975 and 1985 they were harmed by exposure to toxic substances at Spectra-Physics, and that Spectra-Physics failed to warn them about dangers associated with the substances and failed to implement adequate safeguards to protect them from the substances.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2013, the court granted the Company&#146;s motion for summary judgment of Yvette Flores&#146; claims on the grounds that they were barred by the exclusivity of the State of California&#146;s workers&#146; compensation system.&#160; In July&nbsp;2013, the Company reached an agreement with Mark Flores to settle his claims, which were then the only claims remaining in the suit.&#160; In September&nbsp;2013, the Company entered into a Settlement Agreement and Release with Mark Flores documenting the specifics of the settlement.&#160; The settlement amounts were paid in 2013 from coverage by applicable insurance policies. As such, this settlement did not have any net impact on the Company&#146;s income, cash flows or stockholders&#146; equity.&#160; An Order of Dismissal was filed in December&nbsp;2013 with respect to Mark Flores&#146; claims, ending his case against the Company and Spectra-Physics.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In November&nbsp;2012, the Company reached an agreement with Linda Pope and Tia Pope Hudson to settle all claims related to their portion of the suit.&#160; The settlement amount was paid in February&nbsp;2014 from coverage by applicable </font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-29<a name="PB_29_042622_5335"></a></font></p>

<td width="1%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;border:none;border-bottom:double windowtext 2.25pt;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:1.3%;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">$</font></p>    </td>
<td width="12%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;border:none;border-bottom:double windowtext 2.25pt;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:12.46%;">
<p align="right" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">11,424</font></p>    </td>
<td width="1%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;border:none;border-bottom:double windowtext 2.25pt;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:1.22%;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>    </td>   </tr>  </table>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In assessing the realizability of deferred tax assets, management considers whether it is more likely than not that some portion or all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized.&#160; The ultimate realization of deferred tax assets is dependent upon the generation of future taxable income during the periods in which those temporary differences become deductible.&#160; Management considers taxable income in carryback years, the scheduled reversal of deferred tax liabilities (exclusive of deferred tax liabilities related to indefinite lived intangibles), tax planning strategies and projected future taxable income in making this assessment.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company had previously established a valuation allowance against substantially all domestic and certain foreign deferred tax assets due to the uncertainty as to the timing and ultimate realization of those assets.&#160; During 2011, the Company recorded a reduction in its valuation allowance, representing substantially all of the valuation</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-31<a name="PB_31_044100_2897"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>

<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NEWPORT CORPORATION</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">January&nbsp;3, 2015</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">allowance against its U.S. deferred taxes.&#160; During 2012, the Company released $1.8 million of its valuation allowance related to certain domestic deferred tax assets due to the recovery of certain investments and capital loss carryovers.&#160; Also during 2012, after evaluating all positive and negative facts, the Company determined that it was not more likely than not that the Company would realize certain deferred tax assets associated with its former Ophir Division.&#160; Therefore, the Company recorded a valuation allowance of $1.9 million, substantially all of which was applicable to the Optical Metrology Ltd. subsidiary based in Jerusalem,&nbsp;Israel.&#160; In 2013, the Company reduced its valuation allowance by $0.9 million, due primarily to Optical Metrology Ltd. qualifying for the beneficial tax rate of 0% on a portion of its earnings, which necessitated an adjustment to the underlying deferred tax assets and a corresponding adjustment to the valuation allowance.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of January&nbsp;3, 2015, the Company could not determine that it is more likely than not that deferred tax assets related to domestic unrealized losses, certain domestic and foreign net operating loss carryforwards and other miscellaneous foreign deferred tax assets would be realized.&nbsp; Therefore, the Company has maintained a valuation allowance of $2.5 million against its domestic and certain foreign subsidiaries&#146; deferred tax assets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At January&nbsp;3, 2015, the Company had gross state and foreign net operating loss carryforwards totaling approximately $17.4 million and $9.9 million, respectively.&#160; State net operating loss carryforwards begin to expire in 2016, net operating losses of the Company&#146;s subsidiary in Romania begin to expire in 2019, and a majority of the remaining foreign net operating loss carryforwards may be carried forward indefinitely.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At January&nbsp;3, 2015, the Company had federal and state income tax credit carryforwards of $15.1 million and $12.2&nbsp;million, respectively.&#160; Certain unused federal carryforwards will begin to expire in 2017 and will continue to expire in future years if not fully utilized.&#160; The state carryforwards do not expire.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company recognizes excess tax benefits associated with share-based compensation to stockholders&#146; equity only when realized.&#160; When assessing whether excess tax benefits relating to share-based compensation have been realized, the Company follows the with-and-without approach excluding any indirect effects of the excess tax deductions.&#160; Under this approach, excess tax benefits related to share-based compensation are not deemed to be realized until after the utilization of all other tax benefits available to the Company.&#160; During the years ended January&nbsp;3, 2015 and December&nbsp;28, 2013, the Company realized $6.4 million and $4.0 million, respectively, of such excess tax benefits and, accordingly, recorded a corresponding increase in capital in excess of par value.&#160; As of January&nbsp;3, 2015, the Company had $12.4 million of unrealized excess tax benefits associated with share-based compensation.&#160; These tax benefits, if and when realized, will be accounted for as an increase in capital in excess of par value rather than as a reduction in the provision for income taxes.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">If the Company has an &#147;ownership change&#148; as defined under the Internal Revenue Code, utilization of its net operating loss and tax credit carryforwards may be subject to an annual limitation against taxable income in future periods.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Undistributed earnings of the Company&#146;s historic and acquired foreign subsidiaries for which no federal or state liability has been recorded totaled $46.7 million and $32.9 million at January&nbsp;3, 2015 and December&nbsp;28, 2013, respectively.&#160; These undistributed earnings are considered to be indefinitely reinvested.&#160; Accordingly, no provision for federal and state income taxes or foreign withholding taxes has been provided on such undistributed earnings. Determination of the potential amount of unrecognized deferred federal and state income tax liability and foreign withholding taxes is not practicable because of the complexities associated with this hypothetical calculation; however, unrecognized foreign tax credits would be available to reduce some portion of the federal liability.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;28, 2013, the Company had $17.4 million of gross unrecognized tax benefits and a total of $14.4 million of net unrecognized tax benefits, which, if recognized, would affect the effective tax rate.&#160; Interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits were not significant as of December&nbsp;28, 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of January&nbsp;3, 2015, the Company had $17.6 million of gross unrecognized tax benefits and a total of $14.3 million of net unrecognized tax benefits, which, if recognized, would affect the effective tax rate.&#160; Interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits were not significant as of January&nbsp;3, 2015.&#160; The Company believes that gross unrecognized tax benefits may decrease by $0.9 million over the next twelve months.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 12&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; STOCKHOLDERS&#146; EQUITY TRANSACTIONS</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In May&nbsp;2008, the Board of Directors approved a share repurchase program, authorizing the purchase of up to 4.0 million shares of the Company&#146;s common stock.&#160; Purchases may be made under this program from time to time in the open market or in privately negotiated transactions, and the timing and amount of the purchases will be based on factors including the Company&#146;s share price, cash balances, expected cash requirements and general business and market conditions.&#160; During 2014, the Company repurchased 0.6 million shares for a total of $10.3&nbsp;million under this program.&#160; No purchases were made under this program during 2013 or 2012.&#160; As of January&nbsp;3, 2015, 3.3 million shares remained available for purchase under the program.&#160; The terms of the Credit Agreement permit the Company to purchase shares under the repurchase program, subject to certain conditions and limitations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2014, 2013 and 2012, the Company cancelled 0.1 million, 0.1 million and 0.2 million shares of common stock underlying restricted stock units, respectively, in payment by employees of taxes owed upon the vesting of restricted stock units issued to them under the Company&#146;s stock incentive plans.&#160; The value of these shares totaled $2.9 million, $2.0 million and $3.1 million, respectively, at the time they were cancelled.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></b></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 13&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; FAIR VALUE MEASUREMENTS</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ASC 820-10, <i>Fair Value Measurement,</i> requires that for any assets and liabilities stated at fair value on a recurring basis in the Company&#146;s financial statements, the fair value of such assets and liabilities be measured based on the price that would be received from selling an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date.&#160; Level 1 asset and liability values are derived from quoted prices in active markets for identical assets and liabilities and Level 2 asset and liability values are derived from quoted prices in inactive markets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s assets measured at fair value on a recurring basis are categorized in the table below based upon their level within the fair value hierarchy as of January&nbsp;3, 2015.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 14&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; EMPLOYEE BENEFIT PLANS</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Defined Contribution Plan</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company sponsors certain 401(k)&nbsp;defined contribution plans.&#160; Generally, all U.S. employees are eligible to participate in and contribute to one of these plans.&#160; The Company makes certain matching contributions to these plans based on participating employees&#146; contributions to the plans and their total compensation.&#160; Expense recognized for the plans totaled $5.0 million, $4.8 million and $4.8 million for 2014, 2013 and 2012, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Defined Benefit Pension Plans</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has defined benefit pension plans covering substantially all full-time employees in France, Germany,&nbsp;Israel and Japan.&#160; In addition, the Company has certain pension liabilities relating to former employees of the Company in the United Kingdom. The German plan is unfunded, as permitted under the plan and applicable laws. For financial reporting purposes, the calculation of net periodic pension costs was based upon a number of actuarial assumptions, including a discount rate for plan obligations, an assumed rate of return on pension plan assets and an </font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-35<a name="PB_35_074625_7056"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s Israeli plans account for the deferred vested benefits using the shut-down method of accounting, which resulted in assets of $11.1 million and $11.5 million and vested benefit obligations of $12.5 million and $12.8 million being reported on a gross basis as of January&nbsp;3, 2015 and December&nbsp;28, 2013, respectively.&#160; Under the shut-down method, the liability is calculated as if it was payable as of each balance sheet date, on an undiscounted basis.&#160; At December&nbsp;28, 2013, the United Kingdom plan was overfunded and had assets of $3.3 million and a projected benefit obligation of $3.1 million, and all other plans were underfunded and had combined assets of $5.9 million and combined projected benefit obligations of $20.6 million.&#160; As January&nbsp;3, 2015, all other plans, including the United Kingdom plan, were underfunded and had combined assets of $8.1 million and combined projected benefit obligations of $24.5 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At January&nbsp;3, 2015, the aggregate projected benefit obligations, accumulated benefit obligations and fair value of plan assets were $37.0 million, $34.7 million and $8.1 million, respectively.&#160; At December&nbsp;28, 2013, the aggregate projected benefit obligations, accumulated benefit obligations and fair value of plan assets were $36.4 million, $33.7 million and $9.2 million, respectively.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NEWPORT CORPORATION</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">January&nbsp;3, 2015</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">will be sufficient to cover expected liabilities.&#160; The expected long-term rate of return on these assets is 4.8%, which is a combination of long dated government and corporate bond yields for the bond funds, and long dated government and corporate bond yields with an allowance for out-performance for equity funds.&#160; In France, assets are invested in group insurance contracts and the expected long-term rate of return on these assets is 1.3%, which is based on the expected return on the underlying assets.&#160; The Company does not invest in derivative instruments, although the pooled funds it owns may use such instruments in a risk management capacity.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Other Pension-Related Assets</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of January&nbsp;3, 2015 and December&nbsp;28, 2013, the Company had assets with an aggregate market value of $6.1 million and $6.9 million, respectively, which it has set aside in connection with its German pension plans.&#160; These assets are invested in group insurance contracts through the insurance companies administering these plans, in accordance with applicable pension laws.&#160; The German contracts have a guaranteed minimum rate of return ranging from 2.25% to 4.25%, depending on the contract.&#160; Because these assets were not separate legal assets of the pension plan, they were not included in the Company&#146;s plan assets shown above.&#160; However, the Company has designated such assets to pay pension benefits.&#160; Such assets are included in <i><font style="font-style:italic;">investments and </font>other assets</i> in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s Israeli plans are accounted for using the shut-down method of accounting.&#160; As a result, plan assets are reported separate from the net underfunded pension liability and were not included in the Company&#146;s plan assets shown above.&#160; The Israeli assets are invested in government regulated pension funds, which invest primarily in bonds.&#160; As of January&nbsp;3, 2015 and December&nbsp;28, 2013, the aggregate market value of these assets was $11.1&nbsp;million and $11.5 million, respectively.&#160; Such assets are included in <i><font style="font-style:italic;">investments and </font>other assets</i> in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Fair Value Measurements</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The carrying amount of cash and cash equivalents approximates fair value due to the short-term maturities of these instruments.&#160; The fair value of bond funds is based on quoted prices provided by the fund issuer and the fair value of insurance contracts is based on quoted prices provided by the insurance provider.&#160; Because the bond funds and insurance contracts are not actively traded but are valued using observable inputs, they fall within Level 2 of the fair value hierarchy.&#160; Equity securities are included within an equity fund and the fair value is based on quoted prices provided by the fund issuer.&#160; Although the individual equity securities are actively traded, the fund is not publicly traded, and therefore, these assets fall within Level 2 of the fair value hierarchy.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 15</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">BUSINESS SEGMENT INFORMATION</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The operating segments reported herein are the segments of the Company for which separate financial information was available and for which operating results were evaluated regularly by the Company&#146;s Chief Executive Officer, who is the Company&#146;s chief operating decision maker, in deciding how to allocate resources and in assessing performance, during the periods covered by the accompanying financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company develops, manufactures and markets its products within three distinct business segments: its Photonics Group, its Lasers Group and its Optics Group.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Photonics Group products are sold to OEM and end-user customers in a wide range of markets, including the microelectronics, scientific research, defense and security, life and health sciences and industrial markets.&#160; The products sold by this group include photonics instruments and systems, precision positioning systems and subsystems, vibration isolation systems and subsystems, optical components for research applications, optical hardware and three-dimensional non-contact measurement sensors and equipment.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Lasers Group offers a broad array of laser technology products and services to OEM and end-user customers across a wide range of applications and markets, including the microelectronics, scientific research, life and health sciences and industrial markets.&#160; The lasers and laser-based systems include ultrafast lasers and amplifiers, diode-pumped solid-state lasers, high-energy pulsed lasers, tunable lasers, fiber lasers and gas lasers.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 16</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">GAIN ON SALE OF INVESTMENTS</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company holds equity interests in privately-held corporations, which were accounted for using the cost method.&#160; During previous years, the Company had reduced the carrying value of these investments to zero due to the corporations&#146; poor financial condition.&#160; In 2012, one of these corporations was acquired in a merger transaction, and the Company received $5.3 million for its interest as a result of the acquisition, and another of these corporations redeemed its shares from the Company for $1.0 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
